'''Adai''' (also '''Adaizan''', '''Adaizi''', '''Adaise''', '''Adahi''', '''Adaes''', '''Adees''', '''Atayos''') is an [[extinct language|extinct]] [[Native American language]] that was spoken in northwestern [[Louisiana]].

==Classification==
It was once proposed that there may be a connection between Adai and the nearby [[Caddoan languages]], but this now seems unlikely.<ref name="Grant-Adai">Grant, Anthony P. 1995. ''John Sibley's Adai vocabulary: a contribution to Caddoan Lexicography?'' Paper presented at 1995 Siouan-Caddoan Conference, Albuquerque. 15pp. (Contains the entire vocabulary of Adai from MS in American Philosophical Soc.)</ref>

==Vocabulary==
Adai is known only from a list of 275 words from 1804 by John Sibley.<ref>Sibley, John. 1804. ''A vocabulary of the Adaye or Adaize Indians''. Manuscript. (See also Mithridates Vol. 3, part 3., p. 278.)</ref>
